name: 3D Testimonials
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no 21st.dev source was fetched or read, so no MIT attribution is owed. A tilted, endlessly looping testimonial wall is a common social-proof section and costs no dependency: CSS keyframes do the motion and the script only adds the seamless-loop copies.

duration.description: Seconds for one full loop of a row.

gap.description: Space between cards and between rows.

direction.description: Rows scroll sideways, or columns scroll up.

reverse.description: Run the first row the other way.

alternate.description: Every second row runs the opposite way.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside.

tiltX.description: Plane rotation about the X axis, in degrees.

tiltY.description: Plane rotation about the Y axis, in degrees.

tiltZ.description: Plane rotation about the Z axis, in degrees.

fade.description: Fade the leading and trailing edges of each row.

a11y: Each testimonial is in the DOM once for assistive technology: the loop copies are aria-hidden and inert, so they are never read or focused.
Hover and keyboard focus inside the wall pause the loop (pauseOnHover), so a quote can be read to the end.
The loop pauses while the host is off screen, and reduced motion removes the copies and stops the rows; each row then scrolls by hand.
Forced-colors mode draws each card with a CanvasText border on Canvas.
